Michelle Lynn Gill, PhD Applied Research Manager, NVIDIA BioNeMo Team michelle@michellelynngill.com GitHub | LinkedIn | Personal Website Overview I am an Applied Research Manager on NVIDIA ʼ s BioNeMo team, where I lead a cross-functional effort to train NVIDIA ʼ s Nemotron reasoning models for chemistry and drug-discovery applications. My team develops post-training and evaluation data, benchmarks, and metrics that guide model development. Previously, as a Senior Data Scientist and Machine Learning Engineer at BenevolentAI, I applied machine learning to study drug mechanisms and predict ligand binding poses and affinities. Earlier, as a postdoctoral fellow in Arthur Palmer ʼ s group at Columbia University, I developed and applied nuclear magnetic resonance  NMR) spin relaxation experiments to study how enzyme dynamics shape biological function. Education Ph.D., Molecular Biophysics & Biochemistry Yale University, New Haven, CT 2003-2006 Thesis: Development of 205 Tl NMR methods for the direct study of monovalent metal ions and ligands in nucleic acids Advisors: J. Patrick Loria and Scott Strobel M.Phil., Molecular Biophysics & Biochemistry Yale University, New Haven, CT 2001-2003 B.S., Biochemistry University of Kansas, Lawrence, KS 1997-2001 Highest Distinction and Honors  Summa Cum Laude) Experience Applied Research Manager , NVIDIA, Virtual Cell and BioNeMo Teams 2022-Present Lead benchmarking and evaluation of NVIDIA ʼ s Nemotron reasoning models for chemistry and drug discovery Lead benchmarking efforts for virtual cell models, including internal and external collaborations Developed benchmarking framework and tooling for model assessment and reproducibility Collaboration with Chan Zuckerberg Initiative on cz-benchmarks for evaluating virtual cell models
